findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it will never be used as a guard
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer recognizes conditional inclusion methods by the naming convention `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark). Every other guard in this file follows that convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_user_fields?`). Because `include_website_name` lacks the `?`, the serializer will never call it, and `website_name` will be serialized unconditionally—even when `website` is blank—producing a `null` value in the JSON payload instead of omitting the key.

findings.title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking website info for TL0 users
findings.body: The `website` attribute is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), which hides it from anonymous viewers when the profile belongs to a TL0 user. However, `website_name` is not included in that list. Because `website_name` exposes the same underlying data (the website URL's host and path), it will still be serialized for TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors, defeating the privacy restriction that `untrusted_attributes` is meant to enforce.

findings.title: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed redundantly on every branch
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s)` is first parsed on line 138 to extract the host, then parsed again on lines 143, 146, and 149 to extract the path. Parsing should be done once and the resulting URI object reused, avoiding repeated allocations and potential inconsistency if the value were ever to change between calls.

findings.title: No test covers the sibling-subdomain branch (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com)
findings.body: The `website_name` method has three branches: exact host match, same subdomain depth (sibling subdomains), and parent-domain match. The tests cover the first and third branches but not the second (lines 144–146 of the serializer). A test with `Discourse.current_hostname` returning e.g. `forum.example.com` and a website of `http://www.example.com/page` would exercise that path and verify the expected output `www.example.com/page`.
